extracted.intended_audience: professional and amateur planetary observers / astronomers reading a historical observational monograph
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and observational criteria for detecting, measuring, and judging the reality of 'double canals' on Mars — including tests against optical illusion, measurement practices, seasonal behaviour, and corroboration across observers and media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aperture-independence test
rubrics_metrics.description: It makes the width a function of the aperture, decreasing as this increases—which is not sustained by observation. Different apertures produce no effect on the widths of the Martian doubles, as the writer has shown (Lowell Observatory Bulletin, No. 5) by a change of aperture from twenty-four to six inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a suspected double were an optical artifact, changing telescope aperture would change its apparent width; observed invariance of width across large aperture changes supports an objective phenomenon. Example: 24" → 6" produced no width change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idiosyncratic widths (non-uniformity argument)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under like optical conditions the optically produced doubles would be all of a width; while the Martian ones show idiosyncratic widths, each peculiar to itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optical/ocular artifacts should produce uniform appearances; observed systematic differences in separation/width between different doubles argue for intrinsic physical differences and against a universal optical cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility not at the limit of vision
rubrics_metrics.description: These effects are produced only at the limit of vision... the Martian canals when well seen are not at the limit of vision as its framers supposed, but well within that boundary of doubt; so that the premise upon which the whole theory rests gives way. Under good atmospheric conditions the canals are comparable for conspicuousness to many of the well-recognized Fraunhofer lines and are just as certainly there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If features are visible well within resolvable limits (comparable to Fraunhofer lines) and under good seeing, they are unlikely to be retinal/illusory effects that only appear at the visual threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positional invariance
rubrics_metrics.description: In position the lines are invariable, though in visibility not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A genuine feature should retain the same geographic path/position across observations even when its visibility varies. Positional stability (not random shifts) is evidence of physical reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurability of separation (use of micrometer/drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the individual constituent lines vary in aspect and never rise at their most to cognizable breadth, the distance parting their centres, or the width of the double, is quite measurable. The usual spider-threads of the micrometer are colossal in comparison with these filaments... Nevertheless, by means of the finest threads that could be got, estimates of the distance between the pairs were made...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt quantitative measurement of centre-to-centre separation using the finest available micrometer threads and corroborate with measurements from accurate telescope drawings. Be aware of instrument resolution limits and report measurement uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parallelism and great-circle course
rubrics_metrics.description: For a double canal consists of a pair of twin dark filaments, perfectly parallel throughout their course... The pair follow, apparently, the arc of a great circle...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the two constituents maintain parallelism and follow geodesic/great-circle paths; consistent parallel course throughout supports a structured, non-random phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence / canal-specific bilateralism
rubrics_metrics.description: Once shown by a canal, that canal may confidently be looked to at a proper time to disclose it again. In short, bilateralism, or the state of being dual, is an inherent attribute of the individual canal, as idiosyncratic to it as position and size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for canals that repeatedly exhibit gemination across oppositions/seasons; persistence and canal-specific tendency to double argue for an inherent property rather than transient artifact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seasonal behaviour and development stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Schiaparelli deemed gemination a process which the canal periodically underwent. Three stages in the development were to him distinguishable: the single aspect, a short confused aspect, and the clearly dual one... Gemination, then, was a seasonal phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record temporal/seasonal patterns: single → confused (chrysalid) → dual. Note timing relative to Martian seasons (e.g., months after solstices/equinoxes). Seasonal recurrence supports an intrinsic phenomenon modulated by planetary conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flux-driven visibility model
rubrics_metrics.description: Flux, affecting the double canals in whole or part, is the cause of the apparent gemination. According as the flux is partitive or total is a single or a dual state produced... As the flux comes on, one or both lines feel it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat changes in appearance as changes in 'flux' (strength/contrast) of constituents: partial flux can render one member invisible (appearing single), full flux shows clear pair. Use this model to interpret intermittent visibility rather than assuming creation/destruction of structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original (primary) vs duplicate (secondary) asymmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: When the two differ it is always the same one that outdoes its fellow... It is this canal which, except for adventitious help or hindrance from the air-waves, alone shows when the double assumes the seemingly single state. We may therefore call it the original canal, the other being dubbed the duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which constituent is consistently stronger (original) across observations. Use landmarks or connections (embouchures, prolongations) to distinguish original from duplicate. Persistent asymmetry is diagnostic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association with landmarks / embouchures
rubrics_metrics.description: The original always takes its departure from some well-marked bay, seemingly designated by nature as a departure-point, or from a caret belonging clearly to itself; the adjunct, on the other hand, leaves from some neighboring undistinguished spot...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether one member connects to a definite coastal feature, bay, caret, or prolongs into known canals. Such terminus behaviour provides identification and supports physical linkage rather than random illusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement across independent observers and records
rubrics_metrics.description: If the present list be compared with his [Schiaparelli's], the two having been independently made, the concordance of the result will prove striking, corroborative as it is of both. For the necessary observations are very difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek independent confirmation from other observers, observatories, and historical records; concordant identifications strengthen the case for reality despite observational difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Width as a canal-specific norm
rubrics_metrics.description: The widths given are those when the canal was at or sufficiently near its full strength... for different canals the values agree in their difference. This shows that each of these values is, in most cases if not in all, a norm for that particular canal; a value distinctive of it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile width measurements over multiple oppositions; consistent mean widths per canal indicate an intrinsic property. Use mean and year-to-year comparison to demonstrate normativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification by width (narrow vs very wide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two general classes may be distinguished; those up to about five degrees in width apart and those above this figure. Whether such very widely separated lines as go to make up the second class, such as the Nilokeras I and II, constitutes a double is a debatable point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use width thresholds (≈5°) to classify doubles; treat extremely wide pairs with caution as they may represent distinct phenomena or merely parallel single canals. Consider photographic evidence when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: So wide is it that Mr. Lampland succeeded in photographing it as such, the two constituents showing well separated, and if it prove a true double it will be the first Martian double to leave its impress on a sensitive plate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, obtain and use photographic plates to corroborate visual detections. Photographic capture of a double separated beyond visual ambiguity strongly supports physical reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observer training and seeing quality as critical factors
rubrics_metrics.description: More experience than the boys possessed would have helped them to part the sheep from the goats... Improvement in definition has lowered the see-level to revelation of continuous presence of the dual state... Training in the subject and increased proximity of the planet contributing to the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for observer experience and atmospheric seeing: training and better seeing lower threshold for detection. Report seeing conditions and observer expertise when asserting presence/absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development pattern analysis (shading vs true separation)
rubrics_metrics.description: It now appears that in some cases certainly, and possibly in all, the dual aspect is not a temporary condition, but the differing pronouncement of a permanent state, the fact of gemination so called being confined to a filling out of what is always skeletonly there... In some cases a period of swarthy confusion preceded the plainly dual state, but whether the double simply clarified or widened as well it was not possible to assure one's self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish whether a double develops by clarification of pre-existing shaded swath or by real lateral separation. Track changes in the midway shading and edges across time to determine mechanism.
